newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil tax receipts seen up 9.6 pct in 1997-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil tax receipts seen up 9.6 pct in 1997-paper.

text.p: Brazil's Internal Revenue Service expects federal tax receipts to increase 9.6 percent in real terms in 1997 to 113.38 billion reais ($110.08 billion), a financial newspaper said.

Assistant Secretary Lytha Spindola said various factors would contribute to a recovery in tax receipts, including the new so-called CPMF cheque tax, a 0.2 percent tax on financial transactions starting January 23, Gazeta Mercantil said.
The CPMF tax is expected to contribute 4.77 billion reais ($4.63 billion) to next years tax receipts, Gazeta said.
The forecast for 1997 is based on an estimated inflation rate of 10.6 percent and estimated economic growth of 3.9 percent in 1997.

The Internal Revenue Service announced yesterday total tax receipts in real terms for the January-to-October period of 78.91 billion reais ($76.61 billion), down 0.53 percent on 79.33 billion reais ($77.02 billion) in the same period in 1995.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
